text:
Marta: observed a spike of KV-driven OOMs on prod around 10:02 UTC after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. stack traces point to heavy pageflip and a bunch of allocations during long conversations.

Devon: saw the alerts. bump in tail latency too. can you paste the profiler output?

Marta: paste from perf sample (trimmed):
```
KVCache::evict_pages  -> 48%
pageflip_handler     -> 23%
alloc_slab           -> 12%
kernel_select_path   -> 8%
batch_heuristic      -> 4%
```

Liam: looks like the new kernel path increases peak reserved pages for long ctxs. when kv hits eviction, fragmentation spikes and we hit hard OOM instead of soft degrade.

Aria: posted the recent deploy diff: we changed kernel prioritization (favoring quant kernels) and increased max_batch_latency to 12ms. suspect combo increases memory residency per request.

Devon: reproduce locally with long convo load? i can run the longctx loadgen.

Marta: repro steps I used: run loadgen with 1k concurrent sessions, avg length 6k tokens, single model-variant=quant-a, env KVCACHE_PAGE_SIZE=64MB, KVCACHE_MAX_PAGES=120. OOM after ~18m.

Liam: quick mitigation proposals:
- lower KVCACHE_MAX_PAGES to 90 for hosted pool
- enable soft-evict that trims prefix-only pages first
- fallback routing to non-quant kernel for requests with >2048 prefix tokens
- short term: disable kernel-selection tweak on prod

Aria: +1 on soft-evict. We have a soft-evict flag (kv.soft_evict=true) that reclaims clean pages with grace instead of immediate free. It might prevent hard OOMs.

Devon: i ran loadgen with soft_evict=true and reduced KVCACHE_MAX_PAGES=100, repro didn't hit OOM for 40m. tail latency increased 5-7% but stable.

SRE Oncall: can we put an automated rollback trigger? if OOM_count > 3 in 5m, rollback kernel-select change. infra bot can watch.

InfraBot: deploy-watch rule created: name=kv-oom-rollout-watch, metric=kv_oom_count, window=5m, threshold=3, action=rollback-kernel-tweak.

Marta: proposed action items:
1) roll soft_evict to prod pool (canary 10%) - Devon
2) temp reduce KVCACHE_MAX_PAGES from 120->95 - Aria
3) add routing rule for long-prefix to fallback kernel (safe variant) - Liam
4) add perf counters around "reserved_pages" and "fragmentation_ratio" - Marta
5) incident postmortem if OOMs recur after these changes - SRE Oncall

Devon: i'll ship the soft_evict canary in 15m. will monitor kv_oom_count and reservation metrics.

Liam: note for follow-up: we should add a micro-benchmark that mixes kernel selection + longctx to catch regresses in CI. current unit tests don't exercise >2k prefixes.

Aria: created a draft PR to lower max pages and add a flag to prioritize prefix evict in the eviction scorer. PR: https://git.redwood/aws/pull/5421

Marta: logging snippet to help debugging on prod:
```
[KV] reserved_pages=102 free_pages=18 fragmentation_ratio=0.62
[KV] evict_candidate_pages=14 prefix_only=9 tail_locked=5
[Kernel] selected=quant-a sequence_len=6144 batch_size=3
```

Devon: good. i'll attach a small load test to the PR and run it in staging.

SRE Oncall: schedule a 30m watch after the canary goes live. if infra bot triggers rollback, notify #incidents and page oncall.

Marta: thanks all. i'll collect these notes for the post-incident timeline. quick note: prefer "soft_evict + guarded fallback" as our first line of defense rather than broad kernel rollback unless metrics demand it. :white_check_mark:
